fix_text: Where the court order itself specifies a fixed amount, apply that amount as ordered: the employer must comply with the order in its own terms (Función Pública Concepto 251611 de 2022). The employer still retains only 'la proporción determinada por la ley' (Código General del Proceso art. 593 num. 9). In each period, cap the deduction at the garnishable portion of that period's pay: one fifth of the excess over the minimum wage (Labour Code art. 155), or 50% for maintenance and cooperative debts (art. 156). Record any shortfall against the order. This matters in a low-pay period (sickness at two thirds, unpaid leave). Statutory benefits (prestaciones sociales) are not garnishable in any amount. The only exceptions are maintenance (alimentos) and cooperative debts, and even then the garnishment may not exceed 50% of the benefit concerned (Labour Code art. 344). A salary garnishment for any other debt therefore does not reach the statutory service bonus, severance savings or the interest on them.
reason: Verified: the art. 155/156 limits. The T-891/2013 quote ('los jueces solo pueden embargar ... en una quinta parte') is real and is reproduced in Concepto 251611/2022. The art. 344 text and its 50% exception are exact. NOT supported: 'a validly issued order is presumed to already respect that limit' and 'does not need re-testing each period'. The CGP tells the employer to retain 'la proporción determinada por la ley', and T-891 itself ties the limit to the income actually received. In a low-pay month (sickness, unpaid leave) a fixed amount can exceed one fifth of the excess. The no-re-test rule also contradicts the preceding bullet ('apply it to the cap'). Keep the art. 344 content and drop the presumption.

fix_text: Vacation days carry contributions on the last IBC reported before the vacation began, normally the prior month's IBC, not the current one (Decreto 780 de 2016 art. 3.2.5.1). The employee is still paid at the current ordinary rate, and health and pension contributions are due in full on that earlier base. For occupational risk (ARL), vacation is a reportable change event (novedad), and no employer ARL contribution is due for the vacation days (Decreto 1072 de 2015 art. 2.2.4.2.1.6 num. 1.3, from Decreto 1772 de 1994 art. 19 as amended by Decreto 1528 de 2015). On PILA, the ARL IBC may differ from the health/pension IBC when the vacation change event is reported (Anexo Técnico 2, field 44). Función Pública Concepto 091961 de 2022, on public servants, takes the opposite view without addressing that decree article; the decree governs.
reason: The prior-IBC rule is verbatim in Decreto 780 art. 3.2.5.1 ('último salario base de cotización reportado con anterioridad'). The ARL part is wrong in two ways. (1) The citation 'art. 19 lit. c' does not exist; the rule is now Decreto 1072/2015 art. 2.2.4.2.1.6 num. 1.3. (2) The point is not unsettled: that article says 'no se causan cotizaciones ... al Sistema General de Riesgos Laborales' during the vacation novelty. Concepto 091961/2022 says the opposite, but it concerns public servants and is a non-binding Función Pública concept. The same correction applies to the identical ARL sentence in para 5086 (the note after the Module 6 worked example), if that suggestion is in another batch.

fix_text: CONFIRMED: the additional employer contribution is stated in the primary source. Decreto-Ley 2090 de 2003 art. 5: 'El monto de la cotización especial para las actividades de alto riesgo es el previsto en la Ley 100 de 1993, más diez (10) puntos adicionales a cargo del empleador'. So 26% total pension (16% standard + 10 points, employer-borne) is the 2026 rate. Regime validity: art. 8, as extended by Decreto 2655 de 2014, limited the special regime to workers in those activities up to 31 December 2024; workers already affiliated stay covered (art. 8 inc. 3). MinTrabajo Resolución 6072 de 2024 gave operating instructions. Decreto 1435 of 24 December 2025 (D.O. 26-12-2025) extended the regime 'hasta cuando el Congreso de la República expida la ley correspondiente', and it covers workers in those activities 'con independencia de la fecha de su vinculación laboral'. Still open: how the 10 points apply to workers who started a high-risk activity between 1 January 2025 and the decree's publication (no rule found). Configure the 10 points; re-check if Congress legislates (the decree requires a bill within 12 months).
reason: The 10-point rule is verbatim in art. 5. Corrections: (a) The regime lapsed under art. 8 as extended by Decreto 2655/2014; it did not expire 'by its own terms'. (b) 'Res. 6072 protecting only workers already affiliated': Res. 6072 was not read. Decreto 1435 describes it only as 'instrucciones operativas', and the protection of already-affiliated workers comes from art. 8 inc. 3. (c) 'Neither instrument resolves workers hired during 2025' is wrong from the decree onward: par. 1 covers workers regardless of hire date. Only the 1-1-2025 to 24/26-12-2025 window stays open. The 16% base rate (Ley 100 art. 20 as amended by Ley 797 art. 7) was not re-read in this pass.

fix_text: WARNING for any automated severance-deposit build: the engine must compute the cesantías base itself, as monthly salary plus the transport allowance where it is due (Ley 1 de 1963 art. 7; Ley 2466 de 2025 art. 64), and must not copy a figure from any operator or portal calculator. Leaving out the allowance understates the annual deposit for a minimum-wage employee by one month of allowance (COP 249,095 for 2026). A late or short deposit costs one day's salary per day of delay (Ley 50 de 1990 art. 99 num. 3; the statute sets no cap). Ley 2466 de 2025 art. 64 adds two OPTIONAL mechanisms to art. 99. (i) Monthly payment of the 1% cesantías interest directly to the employee: needs a WRITTEN agreement between the parties (par. 2) and is operable today. (ii) A monthly 8.33% advance deposit to the fund (par. 1): depends on MinSalud's PILA regulation, which is not in PILA Anexo Técnico 2 v30 (24-07-2026), and on the MinTrabajo implementing decree, still a draft. Until then the annual deposit under art. 99 num. 3 (before 15 February) remains the operable route.
reason: Verified: the art. 99 num. 3 penalty (one day's salary per day of delay, no cap in the text); art. 64 pars. 1-2; no PILA field for the advance deposit in the v30 annex; the decree is an unnumbered draft. Fixes: (a) the monthly 1% interest needs a written agreement ('Las partes podrán acordar por escrito'), which the suggestion omits; (b) both mechanisms are optional ('podrá'); (c) the ticket reference (HRBS-13692) and the claim about a third-party operator's calculator are ticket findings, not statutory rules, so they belong in the country hub/ticket record, not the CCG. The 249,095 figure (2026 transport allowance, Decreto 1470/2025) was not re-read in this pass.

fix_text: Usually structured as non-salary under a written art. 128 pact, so it stays out of the IBC up to the limit of Ley 1393 de 2010 art. 30: non-salary payments above 40% of the month's total remuneration enter the IBC at the ordinary flat rates. There is no 95-tax-unit or other bonus-specific threshold. If taxable, it is simply added to the month's other labour income for the ordinary art. 383/388 depuration. 95 tax units is the upper bound of the 0% first bracket of the general art. 383 withholding table, which applies to all labour income; it is not a bonus-specific rule and has no bearing on social security.
